messages:
sophie: FYI customer ACME (NL) reporting sudden spike in tail latency + intermittent 401s. They say requests are landing in us-east instead of eu-west. Req id: req_0x9a3b. Started ~2026-03-17T12:10:00Z. Repro steps below from their side.

sophie: curl they ran:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_XXXXX' \n  -H 'Host: api.redwood.ai' \n  -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 88.214.0.12' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-xxl","input":"hello"}'
```

sophie: they also ran: `dig +short @203.0.113.12 api.redwood.ai` -> 34.210.11.3 (us-east IP). Their resolver is 203.0.113.12 (ISP). TTL 300.

tickets-bot: Created INC-5832: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5832 — support assigned to @ryan.

ryan: Can you grab full `dig +trace` output and whether their resolver returns EDNS client-subnet? If ISP is stripping ECS we can get wrong PoP. Also need sample request-id from logs (req_0x9a3b helps).

sophie: Customer pasted `dig +trace` chain:
```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
api.redwood.ai.  300 IN A 34.210.11.3
;; Received 1 IP from resolver 203.0.113.12
;; EDNS: option not present (ISP strips)
```
They confirm ISP strips EDNS.

ingrid: If ECS is stripped, our authoritative sees the resolver IP (203.0.113.12) which may geolocate to US region in GeoIP DB. That explains us-east selection. Two things to check: (1) did GeoIP DB change recently? (2) is resolver in our geoip list mapped incorrectly?

priya: Short term mitigations: ask customer to switch to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 and flush local DNS, or reduce TTL to 30 while we triage. Also consider a per-customer route pin in routing rules (can pin token->eu-west) until fixed.

infra-oncall: Checked our S3 geoip feed — there was a partial rollout 11:47 UTC yesterday; one edge didn't pick up the new db (edge-id: eu-west-02). Pushing hotfix to that edge now.

ryan: Re: 401s — fallback from eu-west to us-east can cause token validation mismatches if auth caches are regional. Logs for req_0x9a3b show 401s at 12:11:03 and 12:11:07, both with `auth-region-mismatch` in header. We should either replicate token store or make fallback proxy auth checks to the home region. Filed a backend task.

sophie: Customer changed to 1.1.1.1 and flushed cache — new dig returned 52.29.44.8 (eu-west) and subsequent requests returned 200 with ~60ms p50. They confirm 401s stopped.

ingrid: Good repro and mitigation. Next steps: (A) ensure all edges pulled geoip DB (confirm eu-west-02 fixed), (B) add alert if edge geoip version lags config by >2m, (C) short-term routing pin for acme token until we have auth fallback improvements.

priya: I'll create a routing pin for acme token and set TTL 30 for 1 hour.

infra-oncall: eu-west-02 DB sync completed at 12:34 UTC. Monitoring for 15m.

ryan: I'll scope auth-region-mismatch fix — either proxy auth to origin region or replicate token validation. Putting draft on INC-5832.

sophie: Customer will monitor next 24h. They were able to continue production traffic after switching resolver. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

ingrid: Action items captured in INC-5832. Adding a diagnostic script snippet for support to run next time (captures resolver+EDNS+traceroute):
```bash
# diagnostic.sh
set -e
ip=$1
echo "resolver: $(awk '/nameserver/ {print $2; exit}' /etc/resolv.conf)"
dig +short @$ip api.redwood.ai || true
dig +trace api.redwood.ai || true
traceroute -m 20 api.redwood.ai || true
```

sophie: Pasting that back to customer and closing loop.
